extracted.intended_audience: SEC registrants (public companies) planning or executing business acquisitions, their preparers, auditors, and accounting/finance teams
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for public-company SEC reporting and related financial-statement and pro forma disclosure requirements when acquiring a business (including timing, significance tests, form/audit of preacquisition statements, and presentation of pro forma adjustments).

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3-05 preacquisition financial statement requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Under Regulation S-X, Rule 3-05, registrants, including entities undertaking an IPO, are required to file the separate preacquisition financial statements for a significant acquired or to be acquired business (acquiree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Registrants must determine whether an acquiree is 'significant' (see significance tests). Preacquisition financial statements generally should be prepared on the same basis as if the acquiree were a registrant. Use judgment to determine whether Rule 3-05 applies to a transaction.

rubrics_metrics.name: Rule 3-14 preacquisition financial statements for real estate operations
rubrics_metrics.description: Regulation S-X, Rule 3-14, may require registrants to provide preacquisition financial statements for a significant acquired or to be acquired real estate operation (real estate acquiree).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply Rule 3-14 when the acquiree is a real estate operation; requirements may differ from Rule 3-05 and should be considered separately when evaluating reporting obligations.

rubrics_metrics.name: SEC definition of a 'business' for reporting purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: Separate financial statements under Rule 3-05 are required only if the acquiree meets the definition of a business for SEC reporting purposes. The SEC definition focuses primarily on whether the nature of the revenue-producing activity generally remains the same after the acquisition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The SEC reporting definition of a business is not the same as the U.S. GAAP definition (ASC 805). An acquiree may trigger SEC reporting even if it does not meet the U.S. GAAP business definition; registrants must carefully evaluate the SEC standard (not rely solely on ASC 805).

rubrics_metrics.name: Distinction from U.S. GAAP business definition (ASC 805)
rubrics_metrics.description: The definition of a business under U.S. GAAP (ASC 805) focuses on whether the acquisition passes a 'screen' test (concentration of fair value in a single asset or group of similar assets) and, if not, whether an input and substantive process were acquired.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not conflate ASC 805 analysis with the SEC reporting/business analysis—both frameworks should be considered because they have different focal points and consequences for disclosure and financial-statement requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Significance tests and financial-statement thresholds
rubrics_metrics.description: The financial information that must be included in SEC filings is generally based on the size of the acquiree, which the SEC refers to as the acquiree’s 'significance.' Significance tests determine required financial-statement periods and thresholds.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Typical thresholds described: significance ≤20% — no financial statements required; >20% but ≤40% — financial statements for most recent fiscal year (audited) and latest year-to-date interim period (unaudited); >40% — two most recent fiscal years (audited), latest year-to-date interim period (unaudited), and corresponding interim period of prior year (unaudited). Use the test that results in the highest significance level to determine periods presented.

rubrics_metrics.name: 50% significance and registration-statement/pro forma requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Registration statement filings must include financial statements and pro forma information for any probable or recently closed acquisitions that are 50 percent or greater in significance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider both individually significant transactions and the aggregate significance of individually insignificant acquisitions (see aggregate significance). If aggregate significance of probable/consummated acquisitions since the end of the registrant’s most recently presented fiscal year is 50% or greater, pro forma financial information must be provided.

rubrics_metrics.name: Aggregate significance of individually insignificant acquisitions
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must consider the aggregate significance of individually insignificant acquisitions that are probable and consummated since the end of the registrant’s most recently presented fiscal year; pro forma financial information must be provided if the aggregate significance is 50 percent or greater.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Track and aggregate small acquisitions undertaken or probable between reporting dates to determine whether their combined effect triggers pro forma and other disclosure requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form and basis of preacquisition financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Preacquisition financial statements of the acquiree are generally prepared on the same basis as if the acquiree were a registrant, but a nonpublic acquiree does not need to comply with certain accounting principles or disclosure requirements that apply only to public companies (e.g., segment or earnings-per-share disclosures).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significant acquirees whose financial statements are included in a registrant’s filing under Rule 3-05 are considered PBEs under U.S. GAAP and therefore should use PBE adoption dates and disclosure requirements. However, the SEC staff said it would not object to certain PBEs electing non-PBE effective dates solely for adopting ASC 606 and ASC 842. Ensure consistency with PBE rules and consider practical relief the SEC staff has indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Audit and review expectations for preacquisition financial statements
rubrics_metrics.description: Generally, the annual financial statements for a significant acquisition may be audited in accordance with AICPA standards. If an acquired company is identified as a predecessor, however, the audit may need to be performed in accordance with PCAOB standards. SEC regulations do not require registrants to audit or review interim financial statements provided under Rule 3-05.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Although not required by SEC regs for interim periods, underwriters often require an independent auditor review of interim information for due-diligence or comfort-letter purposes. Assess whether the acquiree can make audited annual and unaudited interim financial statements available in the required timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing of information and Form 8-K deadlines
rubrics_metrics.description: A registrant must file an initial Form 8-K within four business days of the consummation of a significant business acquisition. The registrant generally has an additional 71 calendar days to file an amended Form 8-K that contains the financial statements required, including pro forma financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Plan acquisition closings and disclosure timelines to meet the 4-business-day initial filing and the 71-calendar-day window for providing required financial statements and pro forma information; consider whether financing or securities offerings change timing needs.

rubrics_metrics.name: Financing preconsummation may require earlier disclosure
rubrics_metrics.description: If a registrant completes an offering of securities before the consummation of the business acquisition to raise capital, the acquiree’s financial statements and related pro forma financial information may need to be provided before the acquisition is consummated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Coordinate financings and registration statements with acquisition reporting obligations so required acquiree financials/pro forma information are timely and complete for the offering materials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Form S-4 and proxy-statement filing differences
rubrics_metrics.description: The acquiree’s financial statements and related pro forma financial information may be required in registration statements on Form S-4 and in proxy statements, depending on which organization’s shareholders must approve the transaction and the nature of the consideration (cash only, cash and equity, or equity only).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Financial-statement requirements for an acquiree in a Form S-4 or proxy statement may differ from Rule 3-05. A registrant may need to provide additional disclosures for the acquiree (e.g., management’s discussion and analysis). Analyze which filing vehicle applies and confirm its specific requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Pro forma financial information — required content and permissible management adjustments
rubrics_metrics.description: A pro forma balance sheet and income statement are generally required under SEC rules if the business acquisition is deemed to be significant. In addition to required transaction accounting adjustments, a registrant may choose to present management’s adjustments in the explanatory notes to the pro forma financial information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Management adjustments reflect synergies and dis-synergies identified by management (e.g., closing facilities, discontinuing product lines, terminating employees). Such adjustments that do not qualify as transaction accounting adjustments should be reconciled and disclosed; when synergies are presented, any related dis-synergies must also be presented. Distinguish transaction accounting adjustments (required) from management’s pro forma adjustments (optional but must be disclosed and explained).

rubrics_metrics.name: Updating acquiree information in future filings
rubrics_metrics.description: An SEC registrant may be required to update the acquiree’s financial statements and related pro forma financial information in future registration statements and amended registration statements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider the obligation to refresh acquiree financials and pro forma disclosures for subsequent registration statements or amendments, and plan for timing and audit/review needs to support updates.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use judgment and consider key questions early
rubrics_metrics.description: Registrants must often use judgment to determine their SEC reporting and public-company acquisition disclosure requirements for a transaction; certain questions should be considered in making this determination (e.g., business definition, significance, form/timing of available financial statements).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Gather key information up front (e.g., whether the acquiree is a business under SEC rules, availability of audited/unaudited periods, expected significance levels) because preparing and auditing financial statements can take significant time and effort and may affect deal negotiations and timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Application of ASU 2024-03 (DISE) to acquiree financials
rubrics_metrics.description: ASU 2024-03 requires the disaggregation of income statement expenses (DISE) for PBEs. Companies whose financial statements are included in another entity’s SEC filing, including those prepared under Rules 3-05 and 3-14, meet the definition of PBE and will be required to apply the DISE disclosures.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: DISE does not change face-of-statement expense captions but requires specified disaggregation in footnote disclosures. Registrants and acquirees whose financials are included in filings should evaluate incremental disclosure requirements and references (see Deloitte Heads Up) when preparing preacquisition statements.
